name: Do Won Kim
roles: PhD Candidate in Information, University of Maryland
Advised by Giovanni Luca Ciampaglia and Cody Buntain
bio: I am a computational social scientist studying how AI and digital information environments shape people’s beliefs and behavior—and how we can redesign these environments to support informed decision-making and strengthen democracy.

In my dissertation, I combine experiments with computational methods to design and test interventions to reduce engagement with unreliable sources, bridge partisan divides, and build trust in elections.

I also study the ranking and recommendation algorithms that shape online information environments, in projects such as the Prosocial Ranking Challenge and research on using large language models to align news-feed recommendations with users’ stated values. Beyond political information, I am also interested in how AI is reshaping the production of scientific knowledge.
